title: The Story of a Mother
text:
A mother sat by her sick little child through a winter night. An old man came in to warm himself. She dozed for a moment, and when she woke, the old man and her child were gone. The old man was Death.

She ran out into the snow to follow. Night, sitting in the snow, would show her the way only if the mother sang all the songs she had sung to her child. A thornbush would show her only if she warmed it against her breast, and she pressed it so close that the thorns drew blood. A lake would carry her across only if she gave it her eyes, and she wept them out into the water. An old woman who kept Death's greenhouse wanted her long black hair, and she gave it, taking the old woman's white hair in exchange.

In the greenhouse, where every human life grew as a plant, she found her child's small crocus by its heartbeat. When Death arrived, she seized two other flowers and threatened to tear them up unless he gave her child back. Death asked if she would make another mother as unhappy as she was. He returned her eyes, and showed her in a well the two possible futures for her child: one full of happiness, one full of misery and fear.

Not knowing which was her child's, she fell to her knees and prayed not to be heard if she asked against God's will. Death then carried her child away to the unknown land.
lesson: Love will give almost anything for a child. But sometimes the last act of love is to accept what we cannot control.
people: A mother, Death, Night, an old woman
source: Hans Christian Andersen, The Story of a Mother (Historien om en Moder), 1847
